As we add `AuthenticatorName` to the Authorizer interface, would you be ok with returning all previous authorizers' errors here as well, using the aggregate `utilerrors.NewAggregate(errlist)`, where each entry would be of form 
```
fmt.Errorf("authenticator %q returned error: %w", currAuthzHandler.Name(), err)
```

That would make this logic more unified in presence of conditional decisions. It could break someone that compared the error returned by this function today with equality (which is anyways a bad practice), but it should not break people that use `errors.Is`.

`AuthenticatorName` is not needed. I realized later that one must not return any additional previous error for Deny especially, as then the return code is 500, not 403. We log "warnings" if we wanted for non-critical errors though, but that's a more general discussion.

Hmm... wondering if `Authorizer` should be made up of two distinct interfaces so that callers can declare which interface they plan on using.

I considered that as well, but I think it's better that all authorizers implement both, so that we don't push the complexity onto the caller. Otherwise a conditions-aware authorizer first has to try to upcast the authorizer, call the conditions-aware method, and if it gets an error, call the normal authorize.

Also it's very easy to accidentally forget to implement one of the functions for composite/wrapping authorizers, even though the delegate/underlying one supports conditions.

I think keeping everything consistent with both methods, and letting the authorizer clearly opt in or not is the most clear method.
